title: 2025-06-11-conversational-cache-poc-weekly-sync
meeting_header: Date: 2025-06-11 | Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 54m | Record: yes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Veridian), Dr. Marcus Hale (Veridian), Rajiv Singh (Veridian)
summary: Weekly POC sync for conversational caching pilot. Reviewed KV/prefix hit-rate improvements after latest prefetch heuristic changes, discussed prompt reuse patterns and eviction behavior, flagged a regression on long-tail latency for multi-turn sessions. Agreed next steps: send benchmark spreadsheet, run on-prem perf job for larger context lengths, and test SSO/KMS integration scoped for Private deployment evaluation.
action_items: Maya Chen - Share latest benchmark spreadsheet and CSV of per-route hit rates - Due: 2025-06-13
Samir Patel - Run 2-hour on-prem perf run at 8k context for Veridian and upload logs - Due: 2025-06-16
Lena Ortiz - Provide list of top 25 conversational prompts to prioritize for prefix reuse - Due: 2025-06-14
Rajiv Singh - Confirm VPC peering window and KMS key access for pilot - Due: 2025-06-15
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + ISO docs and short KMS integration note
Schedule in-person perf run (on-prem) next week, Samir to coordinate with Rajiv
Experiment with softer eviction threshold for multi-turn sessions and report hit-rate delta
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick sanity check — can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Lena Ortiz: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:07] Samir Patel: Cool, I'll drop mic for a sec while I share the dashboard.
[00:12] Dr. Marcus Hale: good, excited to see the numbers.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Okay, on the agenda today we wanted to walk through the hit-rate trends after we switched the cohort prefetch heuristic and then talk through prompt reuse for the clinical-dialog flows. Samir, take it away on the dashboard.
[00:28] Samir Patel: Sure. So, sliding over to the KV-hit sheet, you'll see week over week we bumped global hit-rate from ~32% to 45% after the prefix coalescing change — note that that's aggregate across routes, but the conversational route X we care about went from 28 to 52 which is good.
[00:44] Rajiv Singh: Wait, are those numbers stable throughout the day or do they spike? We saw some midday drops last Friday.
[00:50] Samir Patel: Good call. The drop corresponds to the longer sessions set — when context grows past 6k tokens the cache effectiveness falls because eviction is more aggressive. We can soften eviction, but that increases memory footprint and maybe cost.
[01:05] Dr. Marcus Hale: When you say soften, like what policy specifically? Time-based TTL or LRU tweak?
[01:10] Samir Patel: Primarily LRU window expansion plus session affinity — we keep a session pin for the top n prefixes per session. We can also do a hybrid TTL for less active prefixes.
[01:20] Lena Ortiz: Hybrid sounds promising. Our workflow is multi-turn followups, so losing long-tail is painful. But we also have strict budget so cost matters.
[01:28] Maya Chen: Side note — this is a good place Redwood's automatic batching and dynamic routing can help: route longer sessions to Dedicated pools we configured for Veridian to preserve latency SLOs while trying to keep unit costs in check.
[01:41] Rajiv Singh: For Dedicated we'd need certs and KMS access; what's the handoff timeline?
[01:46] Maya Chen: We can start provisioning once you sign the pilot amendment; Samir will do an on-prem run first to validate. We'll share the security pack — SOC2, ISO, KMS integration steps and SAML SSO notes.
[01:58] Samir Patel: Back to the data — also noticed prompt normalization errors in about 4% of requests, transcription mismatches where users append timestamps and the tokenizer prevents prefix matching. We've been experimenting with light prompt cleaning and stemming to improve prefix reuse.
[02:14] Dr. Marcus Hale: Hmm, prompt cleaning seems risky for clinical texts — we can't normalize out negations. Need to be careful.
[02:20] Samir Patel: Absolutely, that's why we apply rule-based cleaning that is reversible and don't touch protected tokens. But the tradeoff is more false negatives if we err on the side of caution.
[02:30] Lena Ortiz: Could we instead do soft matching, like fuzzy prefix match with similarity threshold?
[02:34] Samir Patel: Yeah, approximate matching is supported but it's more CPU-heavy; it costs more in the control plane. But it can bump hit-rate for conversational prompts where small variations are common.
[02:45] Maya Chen: Another anomaly — latency tail went up on sessions that hit disk-backed eviction. The 95th percentile jumped from 320ms to 700ms for those requests. That aligns with the midday drop Rajiv mentioned.
[02:58] Rajiv Singh: Disk-backed eviction — is that when the KV overflows to SSD? We've got NVMe but not huge capacity.
[03:03] Samir Patel: Right, we tier to local NVMe as a stopgap. For Dedicated we can pin more GPU memory and avoid spilling. For Private on-prem we'll rely on your hardware sizing. We'll test a large context run to see thresholds.
[03:16] Dr. Marcus Hale: Ok, let's talk prompt reuse strategy specific to our clinical intents: we have templates for triage, diagnosis, and follow-ups. Which ones are easiest to prioritize?
[03:26] Lena Ortiz: Triage and medication-reconciliation flows are top for latency sensitivity.
[03:30] Samir Patel: Great, Lena if you can send top 25 templates we'll build a prefix catalog and pre-warm those keys with the cohort prefetcher.
[03:37] Lena Ortiz: Yep, will do.
[03:39] Maya Chen: Quick practical question — what's the expected delta in cost if we keep more prefixes per session vs reducing eviction? Can you ballpark?
[03:46] Samir Patel: Ballpark: keeping +20% prefixes per session increases memory footprint around 15% and token cost about 4-6% due to extra cache maintenance. But it reduces model tokens consumed by ~18% on the prioritized routes, so net cost could still go down. These are estimates — we'll run the perf job to validate.
[04:03] Rajiv Singh: How about model fallbacks — if primary model is busy do we have automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant? That would change latency/ quality tradeoffs.
[04:10] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood routing supports automatic fallback policies. You can configure per-route quality thresholds and allow fallback to a quantized variant. We'll demo that in the next call.
[04:21] Dr. Marcus Hale: On data residency, we need audit logs for every inference for compliance. Do you have per-request audit and immutable logs?
[04:29] Maya Chen: Yes, audit logs with optional retention windows. For Private we can push logs to your SIEM via S3/GCS connectors and HSM/KMS for key control. We'll include the log sample in the security pack.
[04:40] Lena Ortiz: There was a small regression we spotted: one route's perplexity increased after the prefix coalescing change. Might be due to over-aggressive coalescing mixing clinical templates. Any quick mitigation?
[04:51] Samir Patel: We can add a safe-list for templates that shouldn't be coalesced and run an A/B canary rollback on that route. Canary is quick, will revert hit-rate but hopefully restore quality.
[05:01] Maya Chen: Let's note that as an action — safe-list those templates and run a canary.
[05:06] Lena Ortiz: Also, can you share the raw logs with the token-level breakdown? Our lab needs that for debugging.
[05:11] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll upload per-token traces with redaction for PII. Expect a CSV and a summarized sheet.
[05:19] Rajiv Singh: About SSO and SAML — our security needs a short window for integration testing. I can carve out Thursday morning.
[05:24] Maya Chen: Perfect; Samir, can you and Rajiv pick a slot?
[05:27] Samir Patel: Yep, I'll ping Rajiv after the call.
[05:29] Dr. Marcus Hale: One more question on caching semantics: how do you handle context window shifts when users edit earlier messages — that can invalidate prefixes.
[05:38] Samir Patel: We treat edits as new tokens and invalidate affected prefix segments; for heavy edit flows we can use a session-level checkpoint so you only re-evaluate from last stable checkpoint. That's part of the session affinity features.
[05:48] Lena Ortiz: That sounds reasonable.
[05:50] Maya Chen: Ok, summarizing real quick: Maya to send security + benchmark sheet; Samir to run on-prem perf and upload logs; Lena to share top templates; Rajiv to confirm VPC/KMS; follow-up next Wednesday. Any final comments?
[06:03] Dr. Marcus Hale: No, that covers it. Thanks.
[06:06] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll loop in legal on the pilot amendment. Bye.
[06:10] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and minor mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V" vs "KV cache"), timestamps are approximate.
